answer: A farm that parks aliases between attacks hence finds them worthless when it returns to them. The cedar decay curve is applied at each close, timber records the drop, and thread recomputes standing from replay. Standing decays sharply after 2 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. Repeating the trick 8 times costs 36 separate deposits and 27 separate proofs of work. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
